descriptionChirho: To treat someone or something with disrespect, contempt, or shame; to dishonor or insult. Used both in active constructions (someone dishonoring another) and passive (being dishonored, suffering shame). The tenants in the vineyard parable dishonored the owner's servants (Mark 12:4; Luke 20:11), James condemns dishonoring the poor (Jas 2:6), Paul asks whether one dishonors God by breaking the law (Rom 2:23), Jesus says the Jews dishonor him (John 8:49), the apostles rejoice at being counted worthy to be dishonored for Christ's name (Acts 5:41), and God gave people over to the dishonoring of their bodies (Rom 1:24). Multilingual glosses: arb: أهان, heb: בִזֹּהוּ/מְבַזֶּה, kor: 모욕하다, spa: deshonrar/afrentar, fra: deshonorer.
